context: mass-civil led · river diversion, placement rate & first-filling govern the programme

brief.intro: New to this project type? A dam is, at its core, a very large earth or concrete barrier built across a river, so the schedule is dominated by moving and placing huge volumes of fill or concrete, not by conventional building trades. The river itself is the first obstacle — it must be diverted around or through the works before any part of the dam body can be built in the riverbed. Once the foundation is proven sound and grouted watertight, the dam body rises in a steady, rate-driven placement operation, while a small but safety-critical package of gates, valves and monitoring instruments is built into it. The programme only truly finishes when the reservoir is filled for the first time under close instrumented watch.

scope.name: Access & site establishment
scope.desc: Haul roads, work areas, batching/RCC plants and quarry or borrow-area development for a usually remote site.

scope.name: River diversion & care of water
scope.desc: Cofferdams and a diversion channel or tunnel that keep the river out of the work area during construction.

scope.name: Foundation excavation & grouting
scope.desc: Excavation to sound rock, then consolidation and curtain grouting to make the foundation strong and watertight.

scope.name: Dam body construction
scope.desc: Zoned embankment fill (core/filter/shell) or roller-compacted/mass concrete, placed and compacted in a continuous production sequence to crest.

scope.name: Spillway & outlet works
scope.desc: The chute, stilling basin, intake tower and low-level outlet that safely pass flood water and control the reservoir.

scope.name: Hydromechanical equipment
scope.desc: Gates, stoplogs, trash racks, valves and their hoists — the moving parts that control water through the dam.

scope.name: Electrical & power supply
scope.desc: Control power for gates and valves, site electrical distribution and standby generation for flood operation.

scope.name: Instrumentation & dam-safety monitoring
scope.desc: Piezometers, seepage weirs, inclinometers and a SCADA system that watch the dam's behaviour for life.

scope.name: Testing, first-filling & handover
scope.desc: Functional testing of gates and valves, then a slow, monitored reservoir impoundment before handover to the operator.

must_get_right: River diversion and closure are fixed by hydrology and season — miss the window and the whole programme can slip a year.
Foundation grouting must be substantially complete before dam body fill or concrete can rise past it — a real physical dependency, not paperwork.
Fill/concrete placement rate (m³ per day) is the schedule engine — plan and track it like a production line, not a list of activities.
Protect real time for first-filling and its monitoring; it is a slow, instrumented process, not a switch-on.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Fill/RCC placement is tracked as a production quantity (m³ placed per period) against a planned placement curve, not as a simple activity list. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Excavation, grouting and placement typically run extended hours or a 6-day week to maximise the placement season; concrete/RCC placement is temperature- and weather-sensitive (no placement above/below set limits, no fill placement in heavy rain), so a seasonal calendar allowance is embedded. Hydromechanical erection and commissioning run a conventional 6-day calendar.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs river diversion (a fixed seasonal window) → foundation excavation & grouting acceptance → dam body fill/RCC placement (rate-driven, climbing to crest) → gate/valve installation at the embedded openings → electrical & instrumentation integration → functional testing → reservoir first-filling. Spillway readiness must precede any significant reservoir rise so flood water can always be passed safely.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Hydrology and flood-design data are accepted as final; borrow areas and quarry sources are approved and accessible; a single mobilisation; and foundation conditions are within the geotechnical baseline report. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Dam sites are typically remote, with limited access roads and a single haul-road constraint on plant movement. The placement operation needs a dedicated fleet (excavators, compactors, RCC batching/paving plant) sized to hold the planned placement rate, and river flow/flood-season windows restrict diversion and in-river works to defined periods.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: flood events exceeding diversion capacity, foundation conditions worse than the geotechnical baseline (extra excavation/grouting), placement-rate slippage against the planned curve, and slow or interrupted first-filling due to instrumentation trends. Schedule contingency is held around the diversion-closure window and immediately before first-filling, rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for placement crews and the hydromechanical package — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
